decision_reason: First VALID candidate. 23/23 pass at atol=0.01/rtol=0.01/matched_ratio=0.99; geomean 18.35x over eager reference. Becomes the M0 baseline and current best.
notes: Speedup scales with num_tokens (1->10.6x, 8->~25x) => single-token case is occupancy-starved (only 1 CTA on 132 SMs), confirming plan H2. Next: c003 = M1 split-K over topk with fp32 stage-2 combine to fill SMs, expected to lift the small-num_tokens tail (esp. num_tokens=1). Large per-element rel errors coexist with tiny abs (near-zero outputs) and are absorbed by matched_ratio=0.99; abs max ~1.56e-2. Watch precision if PV stays bf16 under split-K.

hypothesis: Split-K flash-decoding over the topk dimension (grid=(num_tokens, num_kv_splits), one KV tile per stage-1 CTA, fp32 stage-2 combine) fills more SMs and cuts serial online-softmax depth, lifting geomean especially at small num_tokens.
change_summary: Two-kernel flash-decoding. Stage-1 partial kernel: grid=(num_tokens, 16), TILES_PER_SPLIT=1 (num_kv_splits=16 for TOPK=2048/BLOCK_N=128), each CTA does one KV tile -> partial (m,l,acc[H,D]) fp32 buffers. Stage-2 combine kernel: grid=(num_tokens, H), fp32 log-sum-exp merge over 16 splits, guarded all-(-inf). PV still bf16 with fp32 acc.

decision_reason: VALID, 23/23; recorded geomean 22.92x >= c003 21.66x, no regression, so kept as current best. BUT the gain is largely REFERENCE-TIMING NOISE: sol_ms is essentially unchanged from c003 (num_tokens=1 0.106->0.113ms, num_tokens=8 ~0.10->~0.105ms), while ref jumped this run (num_tokens=1 ref 1.34->2.90ms, num_tokens=8 ~2.85->~3.0-3.4ms). num_warps=8 did NOT materially move sol_ms.
notes: CONVERGENCE SIGNAL: sol_ms floor ~0.10ms is now stable across c002(single-kernel 0.119), c003, c004(rejected), c005 regardless of split count or num_warps => the op is launch/dispatch + gather-latency bound at these tiny sizes, not tunable by warp/split knobs. The geomean is dominated by how noisy the freshly-timed reference is each run (ref varies 1.3-3.4ms), which we cannot control. Remaining low-risk probes before declaring convergence: (a) num_stages on stage-1 (2->3/4) for deeper gather pipelining; (b) a serialized ncu profile (never during eval) on num_tokens=1 to confirm launch-bound (low DRAM %, few active SMs) vs any real stall we can attack. If (a) and ncu show no headroom, write SEARCH_COMPLETE with c005 as best. Precision stable (abs<=1.56e-2).

decision_reason: VALID but REGRESSES: geomean 19.88x < c003 21.66x. Shrinking BLOCK_N below 128 hurt small num_tokens badly (num_tokens=1 12.57->7.97x, sol 0.106->0.166ms; num_tokens=2 ~14.7->~12.9x). Small BLOCK_N tiles waste the MMA and add combine/dispatch overhead; num_tokens=8 (BLOCK_N=128, identical to c003) essentially unchanged (~28.5x). c003 remains current best.
notes: CLEAN NEGATIVE: more/finer splits are counterproductive; c003's 16 splits @ BLOCK_N=128 is the occupancy-optimal split-K config (for num_tokens<=8, target_grid/num_tokens>=16 always clamps to max 16 splits anyway). sol_ms floor ~0.10ms persists even in single-kernel c002 (0.119ms) => dominant cost is per-call launch/dispatch + gather-latency, NOT split strategy or acc_buf traffic (acc_buf is only ~4MB even at num_tokens=8, negligible). Also note ref timings vary run-to-run (num_tokens=1 ref 1.26-1.34ms) => small speedup deltas are partly measurement noise; trust sol_ms. Next c005: keep c003's proven config (BLOCK_N=128, 16 splits) and probe num_warps=8 on the single-tile partial kernel to raise per-CTA memory-level parallelism (each stage-1 CTA does one un-pipelined gather; at num_tokens=1 only 16 CTAs are active, so more warps/CTA may better hide gather latency).
